title: NovaCore procurement: MSA/DPA/SLAs/pricing & onboarding
summary: Procurement and legal kickoff to review Redwood MSA/DPA, SLAs, pricing bands and onboarding steps. Customer requested clarifications on data residency, encryption/KMS, audit logs, and a shorter SLA for latency. Action: Redwood to send redline-friendly MSA and DPA, provide SOC2 + ISO docs, draft SSO/SCIM plan, and finalize pricing for Dedicated vs Hosted pilot.
topics: Onboarding timeline and trial Dedicated capacity
action_items: Jordan Park: Send redline-friendly MSA + DPA and summary of common redline requests (due 2027-03-25)
Samira Khan: Share technical SSO/SCIM + VPC onboarding doc and network diagram (due 2027-03-26)
Evan Liu: Provide SOC2 report, ISO cert copy, and security questionnaire answers (due 2027-03-24)
Diego Rivera / NovaCore Eng: Confirm pilot scope (models, concurrency, SLAs) and provide dataset residency requirements (due 2027-03-29)
next_steps: Redwood to circulate MSA/DPA redline packet
Schedule security deep-dive with NovaCore infra team (Samira + Asha + Redwood SE)
Agree pilot pricing and start date
Set up trial access and creds for NovaCore engineers
transcript:
Header: 2027-03-22 15:00 PST | Duration: 54 min | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Evan Liu (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Reilly (NovaCore - Head Procurement), Asha Mehta (NovaCore - CISO), Diego Rivera (NovaCore - VP Eng), Rina Patel (NovaCore - Legal)

[00:00] Jordan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll run through the MSA/DPA, the SLA ask, pricing bands for hosted vs dedicated pilot and next steps. I know Rina and Asha wanted to keep this tight, so we can start with the legal stuff first.

[00:18] Liam O'Reilly: Yep thanks Jordan. We just want to get alignment on the baseline terms and any common redlines so our legal can triage. Also curious about the SLA latency numbers you advertise — Diego is here to validate for engineering.

[00:30] Jordan Park: Great. Quick intros — Samira will handle the technical and onboarding questions, Evan for post-sale and security artifacts. Rina, do you want to set expectations on timeline for legal review?

[00:45] Rina Patel: We're aiming to get a first pass in a week if we have a redlineable copy, and flag the top items. Priority: data residency, retention, indemnities, and the usual liability caps. Also the DPA encryption language — we need KMS/HSM details.

[01:10] Samira Khan: On encryption, we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and we integrate with major cloud KMS providers for Hosted; for Dedicated we can support bring-your-own KMS in your VPC. There's also envelope encryption for token storage.

[01:28] Asha Mehta: When you say "support", can you confirm keys never leave the customer's control for dedicated? We need to ensure that logs and model cache keys aren't persisted outside our key scope.

[01:45] Samira Khan: For Dedicated in a VPC yes, the KMS is customer-controlled. For Hosted we use Redwood-managed KMS by default but we can discuss a separate tenancy or bring-your-own if you need it. There may be a small lead time for dedicated KMS integrations.

[02:05] Diego Rivera: Also latency — your SLA page shows p99 for short seq is 120 ms on dedicated; we need p95 under 100 ms for our interactive agent use. Is that achievable?

[02:20] Jordan Park: Typical p95 numbers depend on model size and quantization. For our optimized runtime on A100/4090-equivalent nodes we frequently hit p95 ~80-110 ms for 2k token prompt with batching disabled, but for guaranteed SLA we'd recommend Dedicated reserved capacity with pinning.

[02:40] Diego Rivera: Are those numbers from internal benchmarks? Any chance they vary by tenant noisy neighbors?

[02:50] Samira Khan: Those are measured internal profiles; Dedicated avoids noisy neighbors because it's reserved. We also offer model variants and automatic fallback to smaller quantized models if latency spikes. Note: prefix and KV cache hits improve p95 a lot for repeated prompts.

[03:12] Liam O'Reilly: Okay which data goes into KV cache, and what's the policy for cache retention and purging? Legal will want to know.

[03:25] Samira Khan: Cache is per-deployment for Dedicated; you can configure retention windows — default 7 days. For Hosted it's configurable but sharing models may use ephemeral caches. We'll include that in the DPA appendix.

[03:42] Rina Patel: Can you confirm audit logs retention and export formats? We require tamper-evident logs for any access to customer data.

[03:55] Evan Liu: We provide audit logs with configurable retention, exports in JSON/CSV, and can integrate with your SIEM via syslog or S3. We also have an immutable log option for Private deployments. SOC2 reports detail the controls.

[04:20] Asha Mehta: Please send the SOC2 Type II and ISO certs. Also a completed security questionnaire — our security team will use that to sign off.

[04:30] Evan Liu: Absolutely, I'll attach SOC2, ISO and the questionnaire after the call.

[04:40] Jordan Park: Back to the MSA — Rina you mentioned indemnities and liability caps. Standard Redwood practice is market-standard caps tied to fees with carve-outs for willful misconduct. We see some enterprise asks for higher caps; we can highlight negotiable areas.

[04:58] Rina Patel: Liability cap tied to annual fees is fine but we may ask for higher for data breach scenarios. We'll mark that in our redlines.

[05:10] Diego Rivera: On onboarding — our plan is an initial 3-week pilot, then ramp. We need to define pilot scale: 10k API calls/day, 50 concurrent sessions, set of three models (chat and embeddings). Can Redwood provide pilot pricing?

[05:28] Jordan Park: Yes, we usually do a pilot pricing package: free credits plus discounted dedicated reserved-hours for the pilot. I can propose two options: Hosted credits + engineering support, or a small Dedicated pool for X hours/day at discounted rate. We'll put numbers in the follow-up.

[05:45] Liam O'Reilly: Important — our procurement needs final pricing and SOW draft to approve the funds.

[05:55] Samira Khan: For the Dedicated option we'll need to know the target hardware (GPU type) and concurrency pattern. Diego, could you send typical sequence lengths and QPS distribution? That helps match bin sizes and quantization profile.

[06:12] Diego Rivera: Yep, typical sequence length 800 tokens, peaks to 2k for long context; 50 concurrent sessions for interactive, QPS about 12 sustained. We'll send an approximate histogram.

[06:25] Jordan Park: Perfect. We'll include a recommended config and expected latency targets with each pricing option.

[06:35] Rina Patel: On DPA specifics — data residency. We need all inference outputs and logs to remain in EU for EU customers. NovaCore has EU users; can you guarantee region pinning?

[06:50] Samira Khan: Yes, region pinning is supported. For Hosted we have EU regions and we can pin traffic there. For Dedicated/Private we deploy into your VPC or region of choice. We'll note that in the DPA appendix for data residency controls.

[07:05] Asha Mehta: Another ask: SSO, SCIM and RBAC; we need to integrate with Okta and have role separation for engineers vs product. Also IP allowlist for admin console.

[07:20] Samira Khan: We support SAML SSO and SCIM and fine-grained RBAC in the console. IP allowlist for admin access is supported on Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we have conditional access controls. Samira: we'll share the SSO integration runbook.

[07:36] Rina Patel: Any third-party subprocessors we need to add to the DPA?

[07:42] Evan Liu: We'll include a list of subprocessors (cloud providers, monitoring, analytics) and we can offer to add a subprocessor annex with notification windows for changes.

[07:55] Liam O'Reilly: One more procurement item — do you do background checks for staff with access to logs? We might require that for some SOC controls.

[08:05] Evan Liu: For Dedicated/Private, we can provide personnel security summaries and offer to include background check attestations where legally allowed.

[08:20] Diego Rivera: On the technical deep-dive side, Samira, can you briefly explain the fallback model behavior when a node is overloaded? We want to avoid silent quality regressions.

[08:35] Samira Khan: Sure — fallback is explicit: we can configure policies to downgrade to a smaller model variant and optionally annotate responses with a quality flag. Rollouts are canaryed and traces are available. We expose trace IDs so you can reconcile if quality was impacted. There is also an automatic retry policy parameter.

[08:59] Rina Patel: For legal, we prefer transparent fallback policies documented in the SLA appendix. We'll request explicit notification thresholds for fallbacks.

[09:12] Jordan Park: Noted. We'll produce an SLA appendix showing uptime targets, latency SLOs per model class, fallback policies, and notification/rate of reduction thresholds.

[09:25] Liam O'Reilly: Pricing: do you have enterprise volume discounts? Also any commitment terms for Dedicated?

[09:35] Jordan Park: Yes, Dedicated is sold as reserved capacity with monthly or annual commits. Discounts scale with commit level and GPU counts. For pilots we typically do a month-to-month with a lower commit. We'll include an example pricing table.

[09:50] Diego Rivera: Will there be a penalty or credits if SLA misses occur?

[09:57] Jordan Park: We offer service credits for uptime misses per the SLA. For latency SLOs we have credit tiers or remediation playbooks. We'll include the credit formulas in the SLA appendix.

[10:10] Asha Mehta: Do you encrypt the KV cache at rest and in transit? How are keys rotated?

[10:20] Samira Khan: Yes encrypted in transit via TLS, at rest via our storage encryption; for customer-managed KMS key rotation is under customer control. For Redwood-managed keys we rotate on a regular cadence and can provide rotation logs.

[10:34] Rina Patel: Please include any limitations for eDiscovery/subpoena responses in the MSA — who has access to raw logs and under what authority.

[10:45] Jordan Park: We'll add a section clarifying retention, access, and legal request handling, including notification windows where allowed.

[10:55] Liam O'Reilly: Anything else on procurement side? I want to confirm the sprint for approvals: if we get the redline by Friday, our legal hopes to return comments by next Thursday. Does that timeline work?

[11:06] Rina Patel: Yes, we've budget approval on the 2nd week of April if terms align.

[11:12] Jordan Park: We'll aim to send a redline packet by 2027-03-25. Evan will attach SOC2/ISO and security questionnaire by 2027-03-24. Samira will supply SSO and VPC runbooks by 2027-03-26. Diego to provide load histogram by 2027-03-24.

[11:30] Diego Rivera: We'll also want an engineer-to-engineer session to validate latency numbers and run a short benchmark. Can we schedule that in the pilot week one?

[11:40] Samira Khan: Yes, we can do an SE-led benchmark the first week of pilot and provide tooling. We'll coordinate on times.

[11:50] Jordan Park: Quick recap of next steps and owners — and we'll leave a note about commonly negotiated MSA items so you can triage quickly. Any final Qs?

[12:02] Asha Mehta: No further Qs from security right now.

[12:08] Rina Patel: Nope, thanks. We'll review the redline and flag priority items.

[12:15] Liam O'Reilly: Thanks team, looking forward.

[12:20] Jordan Park: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the packet and calendar invites for security deep-dive and the SE benchmarking session.

[12:30] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions ("K-B cache" for KV cache), speaker overlap, and some auto-caption punctuation errors.
